充 concerns filling, making sufficient, or allotting something to a purpose. In 拡充 かくじゅう, it contributes making provision more substantial; 充てる あてる means allocating a resource to a use.

The modern shape has an upper 亠 and 厶-like middle above the two leg-like strokes 儿, the indexing radical. Modern-shape mnemonic: picture someone standing beneath a sign showing where to allot supplies. This is a visual memory aid, not a historical derivation or a phonetic analysis.

source-only for this quiz: 充たす みたす — fill; satisfy; rare spelling of usual 満たす

All three sourced readings remain in order. Reading questions select ジュウ and あ.てる, not み.たす. The rarity concerns the spelling 充たす, not the pronunciation みたす. For example, 条件を充たす (じょうけんをみたす) means "satisfy the conditions"; normally write 条件を満たす.
拡充 かくじゅう — expansion; strengthening, as of facilities or services
充てる あてる — allocate time, money, or another resource to a purpose
允 has 厶 directly above 儿; 充 has an additional upper 亠 shape.
元 has two horizontal lines above its legs, 兄 a square 口, and 先 a different crossed upper shape. Compare the whole outline.

当てる あてる covers hitting, holding against, and guessing correctly. Use 充てる for the resource-allocation sense taught here, not as a replacement spelling for those contact or guessing uses. The broader あてる family also has allotting uses; this is not an absolute division of every sense between the spellings.
Metadata: KANJIDIC2, 2026-11-02 snapshot. Words: JMdict, entries 1205190, 1334270, 1526670 and 1855580. Meaning and spelling: Jitsu, 充; Daijisen and Nikkoku, あてる.

充てる means allocating or devoting a resource to a particular purpose. Use resource を + purpose に + 充てる: the resource can be time or money. It is a transitive ichidan verb: 充てます (あてます), 充てた (あてた), 充てない (あてない).
余暇を読書に充てています。 (よかをどくしょにあてています。) - I devote my spare time to reading.
ボーナスの一部を旅費に充てました。 (ボーナスのいちぶをりょひにあてました。) - I allocated part of my bonus to travel expenses.
The point is what the resource is used or earmarked for, not simply that it is kept unused in reserve.

充 represents the native stem あ in this allocation verb; てる is okurigana and changes with conjugation. This is one written kanji, not a compound. Its filling/allotting association is a memory aid, not a derivation of the word.

割り当てる (わりあてる), "assign; allot," overlaps in allocating work or resources. 配る (くばる) foregrounds distributing things or placing personnel; 振る (ふる) can mean assigning work to someone. These are related uses, not freely interchangeable constructions.

当てる, also あてる, is the spelling to learn for hitting a target, holding something against a surface, or guessing correctly. Dictionaries also record allotting uses in the broader あてる family, so do not treat these spellings as having completely separate meanings in every context.

In 余暇を読書に充てる (よかをどくしょにあてる), the time is devoted to reading. English "set aside" can instead suggest saving something untouched: 蓄える (たくわえる) concerns storing or accumulating, not this verb's resource-for-purpose relation. There is no single opposite that reverses all uses of 充てる.
Dictionary: JMdict, entry 1334270; comparisons 1207880, 1448860, 1472990, 1361330 and 1596860. Usage and spelling: Daijisen and Nikkoku, あてる, especially Daijisen's 充てる allocation sense.

拡 contributes widening, and 充 filling or making sufficient. Their related contributions suggest both broader provision and greater substance. The on readings are カク + ジュウ. This is a meaning aid, not a history of the characters.
